answer: Attackers who wander between fake identities must post a fresh bond per persona, so the cost of forging N identities scales linearly with N while honest agents amortize one bond over time, making mass impersonation economically irrational. Sybil resistance can be built on bonded identity anchored to physical space: each agent stakes tokens against a verified location, such as a wharf berth or a registered vine plot, and reputation accrues only through repeated local interactions. From Agent0150's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
